title: Why you NEED a goal body
summary: NH argues that every lifter should actively build a personal 'goal body' and visualise it constantly. It works as a distant absolute target, the star, paired with realistic yearly sub-goals, the ladder. The goal must be your own, ideally based on fictional figures rather than real people, and must have no hard deadline, to avoid the 'Arnold effect' of beginners quitting over impossible targets.
claims: Stagnation doesn't exist for humans: if you stop pushing for more, you regress, so maintaining forever is a bad mindset
Shape your goal body actively instead of letting it form passively; thoughts always come before actions
Visualising your goal body works like a golfer's pre-shot routine: picture it, mimic it, then execute
Your goal body should be as ingrained as your birthday, or someone else will fill that empty slot with their ideal
Print or draw your goal body and put it where you see it daily, such as your bedroom or bathroom
Pick fictional bodies for your goal physique (statues, paintings, manga or comic characters), not real people
His own goal body is the 'Buddha physique': big limbs, small shoulders, small chest and a very developed core
Physique preferences are subjective and not up for debate; you don't need anyone's permission to chase what you like
He dislikes big shoulders and would be upset if he were given huge 3D delts, because it would ruin his vision
Very big shoulders compared to the rest of the physique are a mark of enhanced bodybuilders and barely existed before steroids
Question why you want certain features; he wants big arms because he always had small arms and big legs because they look cool
His love of six-packs and core development came from anime and manga, but he made it his own
The goal body evolves as you grow; at 100 lb his goal was naturally not a 240 lb physique
Never set a hard deadline for a goal body; promises like 'a god physique in six months' are marketing, and a good physique doesn't come in six months without drugs
Have an absolute life-long goal body (the star) and smaller yearly realistic objectives (the ladder); you need both
The 'Arnold effect' (credited to Zack Telander) is when beginners set absurdly advanced goals with deadlines, get demotivated within weeks and quit
Perfection being unreachable is a blessing because it means you never run out of reasons to train
Small changes in your absolute goal are fine, but constantly switching disciplines, like athletics to powerlifting to bodybuilding, means you don't know yourself yet
Visualisation is not magic: thinking about your goal keeps you motivated and consistent, and people obsessed with the gym for long periods get the best physiques
People with a clearly defined goal body they deeply want are the ones who stay consistent
His absolute goal body may not be achievable naturally, but chasing it still builds a very respectable natural physique
